facts.factual_statement: Original study: 32 healthy undergraduates, flanker task, startle probes 300 or 800 ms after responses. Error-potentiated startle is defined as mean startle after errors minus mean startle after correct responses, averaged across both lags; the ERN measure is the error-minus-correct difference. Full-sample ERN–startle correlation is not significant (Table 1 magnitude .13); theta and delta associations are separate analyses.

facts.factual_statement: The original labels its median-split analysis Exploratory Post Hoc Data Analysis. Low- and high-ERN groups each have N=16. In the high group, the ERN–startle correlation has extracted magnitude .60 and p<.05; in the low group magnitude .03 and p=.92. This is a within-subgroup association, not a reported difference in mean EPS between high and low groups (the groups did not differ on EPS, all p>.10). The original cautions about the small exploratory sample. Signed statistics are not repaired: the extraction uses U+0002 before .60, .03 and the median 8.25, and represents some Greek symbols as Latin characters.
